What I Learned at My First Tech Conference - Peer Pressure & Developer Soft Skills - Joshua Gawley - ACCU 2025 Short Talks
---

Attending your first tech conference can be overwhelming, especially when imposter syndrome in tech is real. In this lightning talk from ACCU 2025, Joshua Gawley, a final-year computer science student, shares his first tech conference experience and reflects on what it’s like to be a junior developer surrounded by seasoned professionals.

This talk, titled "What I Learned at My First Tech Conference - Peer Pressure and Developer Soft Skills," offers a fresh perspective on software engineering soft skills, peer pressure in engineering culture, and the unexpected importance of people skills in technical careers.
